title: Revisiting Entropy in Reinforcement Learning for Large Reasoning Models
data_curation: Training uses the DAPO-Math-17K dataset with GRPO on Qwen2.5-Math-7B (and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct for generalization). To study how data diversity affects entropy, the authors build subsets of identical size but differing diversity via K-means clustering (K=1,000 clusters on mean-pooled final-layer embeddings of Qwen2.5-Math-7B) versus random sampling, yielding subsets of 10,001, 5,031, 2,538, 1,246, and 616 samples by drawing from the top-M clusters. Key finding: diversity, not scale, governs entropy — K-means subsets yield lower entropy than random subsets, and a model trained on ~616 K-means samples matches one trained on the full ~17K set (Avg@64 ID 45.13 vs 44.12). No new data is generated; subset selection/diversity is the curation lever. EMA-smoothed final-step entropy is reported (smoothing coefficient 0.6).
curriculum: Not a focus of this paper. Training is a single RLVR/GRPO stage applied to a pretrained math model; there is no pretrain->SFT->preference->RL pipeline. The only scheduling is internal to the proposed method: Pos-Adv-Reweight (Stage-based) splits RLVR into two equal halves with lambda=0 (only non-positive-advantage tokens) then lambda rising linearly 0->1; (Epoch-wise) ramps lambda=(e-1)/(E-1) across epochs; (Entropy-guided) adapts lambda stepwise (Delta=0.05, delta=0.2) around an entropy target. These lambda schedules act as a warmup/anneal over positive-advantage contribution rather than a cross-stage curriculum.
method: The paper analyzes and mitigates entropy collapse during GRPO-based RLVR. It identifies three governing factors: clipping thresholds (Clip-Higher raises epsilon_high to 0.28, mitigating collapse; Clip-Lower, Clip-Tighter, Clip-Free are tested), number of off-policy updates per batch (N_update in {1,2,4}; more updates amplify entropy drift and overfitting), and training-data diversity. Through a gradient analysis of the GRPO objective w.r.t. logits and ablations training only on Adv>=0 vs Adv<=0 tokens, it shows positive-advantage tokens drive collapse: they raise probabilities of high-probability sampled tokens while suppressing low-probability unsampled ones, concentrating the distribution. Building on this, Positive-Advantage Reweighting (Pos-Adv-Reweight) introduces a weight lambda on positive-advantage-token losses, realized as Stage-based, Epoch-wise, and Entropy-guided variants. A Rand-Pos-Clip baseline randomly zeros gradients of a subset of positive-advantage tokens. Baselines include Ada-Ent-Reg, Clip-Cov, KL-Cov, and Entropy-Adv.
eval_metrics: Evaluation uses Avg@64 and Pass@64 (64 samples per question, temperature=1.0, top-p=1.0) plus token-level entropy, N-gram Diversity, SelfBLEU, Spearman correlations, and log-prob calibration plots. In-domain benchmarks: AIME 2024/2025, MATH500, AMC 2023, Minerva Math; out-of-domain: LiveCodeBench (coding) and IF-Eval (instruction following). AIME 2025 serves as validation for Qwen2.5-Math-7B, MATH500 for Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. Headline: Pos-Adv-Reweight (Entropy-guided) on Qwen2.5-Math-7B achieves the best average Avg@64 among all entropy methods (ID 45.66, OOD 19.39) and beats Clip-Higher on 6 of 7 benchmarks; AIME 2024 rises to 34.38/73.33 vs GRPO's 28.75/63.33 and base 10.00/60.00. Entropy-performance correlation is task/metric dependent (strong negative on LiveCodeBench Avg@64). Results generalize to Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct.
key_results: Qwen2.5-Math-7B + Pos-Adv-Reweight (Entropy-guided): AIME 2024 Avg@64 34.38 / Pass@64 73.33; best average Avg@64 (ID 45.66, OOD 19.39), beating Clip-Higher on 6 of 7 benchmarks. ~616 K-means-selected samples match full DAPO-Math-17K (Avg@64 ID 45.13 vs 44.12), showing data diversity, not scale, drives RLVR performance. GRPO lifts AIME 2024 Avg@64 from 10.00 (base) to 28.75.
evolution_note: Builds on the 2024-2025 RLVR/GRPO wave (DeepSeek-R1, DAPO's Clip-Higher, Cui et al.'s Clip-Cov/KL-Cov, He et al.'s adaptive entropy regularization) and the covariance-based entropy-collapse theory of Liu (2025) and Cui et al. (2025), refining their positive-advantage-token insight into a directly controllable per-token loss weight. It motivates finer-grained, entropy-targeted token reweighting for forthcoming agentic and long-context RL, noting the concurrent QwenLong-L1.5/AEPO work as a related direction.
